title: Planar diffusions with a point interaction on a finite time horizon
summary: The skew-product diffusion [Ann. Appl. Probab. 35, 3150--3214 (2025)] and exponentially tilted planar Brownian motion [Electron. J. Probab. 30, 1--97 (2025)] are canonical examples of planar diffusions with a point interaction at the origin in the sense that their drifts are singular only at the origin and allow visits there with positive probability. However, in this article we propose an axiomatic framework for such diffusions on a finite time horizon.
